## TL;DR

The review pass history column now reads **Issues** instead of "finding classes". Board cards show the task number as plain text, and the top line (number, type, tags, priority, robot) stays on one row at 375, 768 and 1280 px. The type label "feature" shortens to "feat" only when the full word is clipped. The scoped check passed locally, and the remote validation run passed with 858 tests green.

## Work and rationale

- **Header.** `TaskDrawer.vue` now renders `Issues` in the last `th` of the review pass table. The cell content (reviewer class labels, a dash when none) and the internal `findingClasses` field are unchanged, as the task asked. I capitalised "Issues" because the spec says it should read that way, even though the sibling headers are lowercase. `user-docs/review-and-close-out.md` now describes the column as an **Issues** column.
- **Card number.** The board card used `CopyableNumber`, a bordered button with a copy-link action. It is now a plain `span` styled like the pipeline card's id. The copy-link action is gone from board cards. The drawer's chip still copies, as the task specified.
- **One-row top line.** The row was `flex-wrap`, which is why it wrapped. It is now `flex-nowrap` with a `tc-top-line` class. The number, priority badge, robot button and hotfix badge are `shrink-0`. The type chip and the "needs merge" tag are `min-w-0 truncate`, so they absorb any squeeze. The first version kept the tag at its natural width, and the WebKit fixture at 1280 px caught a `bug` card with a needs-merge tag and a p1 badge spilling out of the card. Letting the tag truncate fixed it.
- **"feat" only when needed.** CSS cannot compare the type label's width with the sum of its siblings, since the id length, the p1 badge and the tags all change the budget. So the component measures. After each render it checks whether the type chip's `scrollWidth` exceeds its `clientWidth`. If it does, the label becomes `feat`. The check re-runs on mount, on `ResizeObserver` callbacks, and when the id, type, priority, hotfix or needs-merge state changes. The `data-tip` tooltip keeps the full type, and only `feature` ever shortens.

## Approaches tried

- **Container queries.** I considered them first and rejected them, because the decision depends on the sibling widths and not only on the card width.
- **Width breakpoints.** Rejected for the same reason. A 220 px card with a short id fits "feature", while the same card with a nine-digit id and a p1 badge does not.
- **Measuring after render.** This is what I shipped. It is one forced layout per card per resize, which is acceptable for the board's card counts, and it is guarded for environments without `ResizeObserver`.

## Challenges and blockers

- **The live switch is not verified in a real browser.** The WebKit harness mounts static markup that jsdom produced, so jsdom cannot run the measurement. In a screenshot at 220 px, the nine-digit `feature-long-id` fixture shows `featu…` as static markup, which the live component would replace with `feat`. I covered the switch logic with a jsdom test that stubs `scrollWidth` and `clientWidth`. I did not run the live component in a real layout, so a human should look at a card in the running app.
- **Hotfix badge.** The hotfix badge is `shrink-0` and has no fixture. A hotfix card with a long type name at 220 px could still spill. This is not covered and I did not change it.
- **Test updates.** `task-card-agent-header.test.ts` looked for the robot in a `.flex-wrap` row, which I removed on purpose, so I pointed it at the non-wrapping top line. `task-card-states-qa-browser.test.ts` injected the `CopyableNumber` stylesheet, which would have silently gone empty, so I removed that injection and added a long-id, p1 `feature` fixture plus a WebKit one-row check at 375, 768 and 1280 px for every fixture. `task-drawer-landable.test.ts` now asserts that the last header reads "Issues".
- **Shot declarations.** The first drawer shot highlighted `.review-history-table`, and the handoff's UI verification found nothing to highlight on `/work?task=9999&tab=review` with the `drawer:reviewPasses` state. The table is gated on the same condition as the round-guidance line, so I could not confirm from the code why the fixture state misses it. I dropped that highlight and kept the drawer shot, so it captures the review tab without a selector. The header itself is covered by the drawer test. The board shot keeps its `.task-card .tc-top-line` highlight. `repoos update` also warned that it read the main checkout's board from the linked worktree, then reported success.

## Key learnings

- A flex row that wraps is easy to detect in a browser test: the row is taller than its tallest child. That check holds across every fixture and does not depend on exact pixel widths.
- For "shorten only when needed", measuring the clipped element is more reliable than predicting the budget from CSS. The rule needs one measured chip and one re-measure on resize.
- A copy-only change still moves layout. The first attempt left a spill that only the 220 px fixture showed, so the fixture matrix is worth running even for small UI edits.
